QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov 23, QQQ’s 252-return DFA H was 0.476, near the independent finite-variance benchmark of 0.5. R²=0.925 measures fit only over tested scales. One line fits 8–63 poorly: H=0.391 at 8–20 versus 0.545 at 25–63, suggesting possible crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Absolute-return H=0.733 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H changed −0.0062/+0.0083 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-30 z-score was −0.22, not a significance test because windows overlap. H/alpha went from 0.520/3.300 (Nov 6) to 0.455/3.380 (Nov 13) to 0.476/3.270 (Nov 23).

Hill uses 1,000 returns (~4 years), k=100, x_min=0.02051 absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. Idealized i.i.d. SE=0.327 understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.274/2.953, not confidence bounds. Unchanged extremes can leave alpha flat without implying stasis. These uncertain descriptive estimates are not a crash forecast.
